description: Fresh EN alpine rescue admission domain.

units.title: Avalanche beacon check
units.text: Each team member performs a transmit-and-search beacon check before leaving the trailhead so a failed transceiver is discovered before exposure to avalanche terrain. The result is confirmed verbally by the team lead.

units.title: Weather reassessment
units.text: When cloud base drops and visibility obscures the planned ridge, the leader reassesses the route instead of continuing automatically. The team may descend or select a lower alternative.

units.title: Cold casualty handling
units.text: A cold casualty is insulated from wind and ground contact before nonessential clothing changes because unnecessary exposure can accelerate heat loss. Wet layers are handled under shelter when possible.

units.title: Rope anchor inspection
units.text: Before loading a rescue anchor, a second rescuer independently checks the attachment points and locking connectors. The haul team waits for that cross-check before tensioning the system.

units.title: Radio discipline
units.text: Critical radio messages are repeated back by the receiving station to confirm that coordinates and instructions were understood. Routine status traffic does not require a full read-back.

units.title: Rotor approach
units.text: Rescuers approach a helicopter only after the flight crew signals that it is safe to do so. Loose equipment is secured before anyone enters the rotor area.
